subject: FinPay — Competitive evaluation & TCO follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: FinPay — Post-demo recap & next steps (cost/TCO tests)

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights
- You’re evaluating inference for live customer-facing assistants (real-time chat) + nightly batch summarization for compliance.
- Key goals: predictable latency under 300ms P95, durable audit logs, and TCO under your internal threshold (target ~$X / 1M tokens).
- Main competitive concerns: hyperscaler ease-of-use vs cost; vendor lock-in; fine-tuning/embeddings pipeline compatibility.

Proposed next steps
1) Redwood to provide a short TCO model for your two workloads (real-time + batch) with configurable assumptions: batching, KV cache hit rates, effective RPS, and model family choices. I attached our working model.
2) Run a 1-week pilot: 10k chats/day production-like traffic + nightly 50k-doc summarizations. Redwood will provide guidance on batching + cache config for realistic unit economics.
3) Provide a short competitive matrix vs CloudAI and HyperscaleX (we’ll call out network egress, latency SLOs, and per-token unit costs).

Questions for you
- Can you confirm the expected average tokens per chat turn (user + assistant) and typical session length?
- Any procurement constraints (PO vs DocuSign) we should prep for?

Attachments: redwood_tco_modeling_finpay.xlsx (working TCO model), redwood-capabilities-one-pager.pdf

I’ll loop Marcus on the cost modeling and Marissa on the pilot coordination.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1-415-555-0193

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finpay.com>

Cc: Tom Lowe <tom.lowe@finpay.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay — Post-demo recap & next steps (cost/TCO tests)

Thanks Aditya — this looks good. A few clarifications below so your model can be accurate: 

- Average tokens per user message: ~40 tokens. Assistant response average: ~120 tokens. So ~160 tokens per turn.
- Typical session = 3–4 turns (user + assistant sequences).
- Peak RPS for chat: ~25 RPS regionally (US-east).
- For batch summarization: nightly job processes ~50k docs, average 450 tokens/doc.

Procurement: We prefer DocuSign for evaluation agreements — legal needs the envelope.

Next: please update the model with two scenarios (optimistic cache hit 40% and conservative 10%) and with batching enabled/disabled. Also include an expected latency impact when batching at 8–16 request batch sizes for the chat workload.

—Sara
Sara Jenkins
Product Lead, Conversational AI | FinPay

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 13:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinPay — Post-demo recap & next steps (cost/TCO tests)

Hi Sara — thanks for the numbers. I updated the attached TCO workbook with the two cache scenarios and batching permutations you asked for. High level summary (per 1M tokens):

Assumptions (chat workload):
- Avg tokens per turn: 160
- Session length: 3.5 turns -> ~560 tokens/session
- Peak steady RPS: 25
- Costing uses Redwood hosted model family variants: rwd-gpt-medium (quantized) and rwd-gpt-large (fp16).

TCO summary (per 1M tokens) — approximate
- rwd-gpt-medium, no batching, 10% cache hit: $28 / 1M tokens
- rwd-gpt-medium, batching 8, 10% cache hit: $21 / 1M tokens
- rwd-gpt-medium, batching 8, 40% cache hit: $16 / 1M tokens
- rwd-gpt-large, batching 8, 40% cache hit: $31 / 1M tokens

Comparative notes vs hyperscalers (CloudAI/HyperscaleX) — quick callouts
- Raw per-token price: hyperscalers are competitive at list price but often omit egress and sustained throughput pricing; real TCO typically 10–25% higher when you model throughput and cache benefits.
- Latency: Redwood’s smart routing + KV prefix caching preserves sub-300ms P95 in our tests even when batching at 8, whereas some hyperscaler endpoints see P95 regress with high concurrency without custom autoscaling.
- Instrumentation & rollouts: Redwood provides per-route latency + token cost breakdowns and can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback to cheaper model variants on errors. That reduces risk during pilot.

Next steps I suggest:
- We’ll run two short tests (3 days each):
  a) baseline: run pilot traffic w/ batching off to measure raw latency and cache effectiveness
  b) optimized: enable batching (8) and KV caching to measure TCO delta and P95 impact

I’ll schedule time with Marissa to coordinate the pilot infra and with Aditya to surface procurement. If you want, we can also loop HyperscaleX contacts to get their benchmark numbers for apples-to-apples.

Attached: redwood_tco_modeling_finpay.xlsx (updated)

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@finpay.com>

Thanks Marcus — all very helpful. We’re aligned on the test plan. Confirming:

- FinPay will approve the 1-week pilot (baseline + optimized) starting Mon 2026-08-24.
- Legal requests DocuSign evaluation agreement — please send envelope to legal@finpay.com.
- I’ll provide a sample production traffic replay (anonymized) by EOD Friday so you can seed realistic RPS and token distributions.

Action items for Redwood:
- Aditya: send DocuSign envelope link to legal@finpay.com.
- Marcus/Marissa: finalize infra steps and pilot runbook; include explicit metrics we’ll capture (P95 latency, tokens consumed, cache hit rate, cost per 1M tokens).

We’re also open to a short competitive ask: if you can share the same three datapoints from HyperscaleX (list per-token price, typical P95 at 25 RPS, and any sustained throughput discounts), that’ll help our procurement comparison.

—Sara
